This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the appellant/petitioner challenging the finding of the Tribunal in fixing the liability on the first respondent/Transport Corporation instead of the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company in M.C.O.P.No.247 of 2010 dated 04.02.2021 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sub-Court, Cheyyar, Tiruvannamalai District.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sub-Court, Cheyyar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The appellant filed M.C.O.P.No.247 of 2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Sub Court, Cheyyar, Tiruvannamalai, claiming a sum of Rs.9,00,000/- as compensation for the death of one Venkatesan, who died in the road accident that took place on 23.05.2010.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Sub Court, Cheyyar, Tiruvannamalai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. According to the appellant, on 23.05.2010 at about 4:50 P.M, when the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider in the Hero Honda Splender Plus _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis bearing Registration No.PY 01 AR 0849, from Vandavasi to Melmaruvathur Road, near Seeshamangalam, a Kartanaka Bus bearing Reg.No.KA 01 FA 993 which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the vehicle of the deceased.
As a result, the said Venkatesan sustained multiple grievous injuries and died on the spot.
The deceased was doing Thari business of his own and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Thus, the appellant filed a claim petition claiming compensation against the respondents.
4. The 1st respondent remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.

5. The 2nd respondent/Insurance Company filed a counter statement denying all the averments made by the appellant in the claim petition and stated that the driver of the bus drove the vehicle with due care and cautious manner, that there was no negligence or rash driving on the part of the Bus driver; and that in any event, the total compensation claimed by the appellant is highly excessive and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.
Before the Tribunal, the appellant examined herself as P.W.1 and marked eight documents as Exs.P.1 to P.8.
The respondents neither marked documents nor examined witnesses.

7. The Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents filed on the side of the appellant,
held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Bus and directed the first respondent to pay a sum of Rs.15,30,600/- as compensation to the appellant since the FIR had been registered against the 1st respondent.
8. Aggrieved by the said order, the appellant has preferred the present appeal.

9. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that admittedly the first respondent bus was insured with the 2nd respondent; that the Tribunal has found that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the first respondent and in such circumstances, the _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2nd respondent who is the insurer of the vehicle belonging to the first respondent is liable to pay compensation; that however, the Tribunal after holding that the accident took place due to the rash driving by the driver of the 2nd respondent and holding that there was a valid insurance policy, fastening the liability on the 1st respondent is erroneous.

The learned counsel further relied upon the Judgment of the very same Tribunal in M.C.O.P.No.186 of Panchavarnam vs The Managing Director on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117985723/
2 2010 filed by another appellant in respect of the same accident wherein the Tribunal found that the 1st respondent is guilty of negligence and fastened the liability on the 2nd respondent as there was a valid insurance policy.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Though notice has been served on the 1st respondent, none has entered an appearance on behalf of the 1st respondent.
11. The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent fairly conceded that there is a valid Insurance policy.
__ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 12

. This Court finds that in view of the submission made by the learned counsels on either side and the fact that there was a valid insurance policy with the 2nd respondent, and the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the 1st respondent vehicle, the finding of the Tribunal that the 1st respondent is liable to pay compensation is erroneous and hence, the same is set aside.
The 2nd respondent/Insurance company is liable to pay compensation.
Both parties have not questioned the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the same is confirmed with the direction to the 2nd respondent/Insurance company to pay the compensation of Rs.15,30,600/- to the appellant.
13. In the result, Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed.

The 2nd respondent/Insurance company is directed to deposit the award amount of Rs.15,30,600/- together with interest at 7.5% per annum (excluding the default period if any) from the date of petition till the date of deposit, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of six (6) weeks from the date of a receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
On such deposit, _____ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
the appellant is permitted to withdraw the award amount, along with interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn.
No costs.
